item.title: The End of Oak Street Draws on an Enduring ’80s-Era Spielberg Formula
item.description: The new Warner Bros. science-fiction thriller, The End of Oak Street, imagines a suburban neighborhood mysteriously transported to prehistoric times, where the unfortunate inhabitants try (and mostly fail) to survive becoming a dinosaur’s dinner. But the presence of velociraptors isn’t the only quality of the film that feels like a product of another era. item.dc:creator: Miles Surrey

item.title: Index Funds Channel Investor Gains to Companies and Insiders
item.description: On the first few trading days of every month, America’s paychecks hit the stock market. Most 401(k) contributions now default into index-tracking funds, which buy the same stocks in the same proportions whatever the price. New research shows this tide measurably lifts the funds that hug the index and sinks the managers who dare to deviate from it; a few basis points at the turn of each month, every month, for 15 years running.
item.dc:creator: Aaron Brown

item.title: Moderna and Merck's Melanoma Vaccine Is the Cancer Advance We Needed
item.description: Scientists are on the cusp of fulfilling a decades-long quest: to use vaccines to teach the immune system to spot and destroy cancer cells.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Jarvis

item.title: US Automakers Need More Than Peace With Canada
item.description: The US and Canada appear poised to clinch a deal on an industry central to the North American free-trade battle: autos. As ever with President Donald Trump’s trade war, a fog of uncertainty and potential U-turns persists. In this case, the details that have emerged suggest the deal would represent a good first step for Detroit, but only that. Don’t tell the president, but foreign automakers look like more immediate beneficiaries.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: Federal Reserve Undermined by Treasury’s Aggressive Buyback Strategy
item.description: That was quicker than anyone surely imagined. It’s been just three months since Kevin Warsh took the helm of the Federal Reserve and he’s already being undermined by a White House that gave him the job.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin
